guidance: Measure each wheel across the tyre where the blade rides and take the axle spacing with the tensioner at the middle of its travel, then order a stock length near the middle of the saw's range so the tensioner can take up stretch and slacken the blade for storage. Check the number against the saw's manual before ordering.
method: A band saw blade is a closed loop over two wheels: two straight runs and one arc on each wheel. With wheel diameters D1 and D2 and the axle spacing C, the exact open-belt length is 2 sqrt(C^2 - ((D1 - D2)/2)^2) + (pi + 2t) D1/2 + (pi - 2t) D2/2, where t = asin((D1 - D2)/(2C)) and D1 is the larger wheel, so the larger wheel is wrapped through 180 + 2t degrees and the smaller through 180 - 2t. For equal wheels this reduces to 2C + pi D. The shop rule 2C + pi (D1 + D2)/2 + (D1 - D2)^2/(4C) is the same geometry expanded, and differs from the exact wrap by under 0.001 in for wheels within a few inches of each other and by about 0.02 in for a 40 in wheel driving a 10 in wheel 60 in away. Given a blade length instead of a spacing, the calculator solves the same expression for C by bisection between the touching-wheel spacing, where the blade is at its shortest possible length, and the spacing at which that length fits; a blade shorter than that minimum is refused, and a required spacing above 120 in (3048 mm) is refused as outside a saw. Wheel diameters are accepted from 4 to 40 in (102 to 1016 mm), a spacing up to 120 in, and a blade from 15 to 450 in (381 to 11430 mm); a spacing no greater than the two wheel radii added together is refused because the wheels would overlap. Every length is reported in inches and millimetres, the blade length is also rounded to the nearest 1/8 in, and the report gives each straight run, the wrap on each wheel, and the blade length change per unit of wheel travel, which is twice the straight run divided by the spacing and is exactly 2 for equal wheels. Moving the upper wheel by x therefore changes the blade length by about 2x, which is why a saw accepts a band of lengths rather than one figure. The model assumes a two-wheel saw with plain tyres and coplanar wheels; it does not model three-wheel saws, crowned or stepped tyres, blade thickness, wheel tilt, or the tensioner's actual travel, so the result has to be checked against the saw's manual, and it is an ordering aid rather than a claim about the saw.

sources.title: Highland Woodworking, Bandsaw Blade Length: with no blade fitted, twice the shaft-to-shaft distance plus one wheel circumference (diameter times pi) gives the blade length, and the same sum taken at the top and bottom of the tensioner travel gives the range of lengths the saw will mount.

Wikipedia, Belt (mechanical): an open belt is two straight runs plus half the circumference of each pulley, with the difference of the radii adding a correction, so unequal bandsaw wheels need a slightly longer blade than the equal-wheel sum.
